verifications.claim: Artemis II is scheduled to return to Earth on Friday, April 10, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'Orion will come home Friday (April 10)'; R3: 'splashdown ... at 8:07 p.m. EDT ... April 10'; R4: 'splash down ... on Friday, April 10'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly state splashdown/return on April 10, 2026, explicitly Friday in R2 and R4.

verifications.claim: Artemis II is scheduled to splash down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego, CA.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'splashdown off the coast of San Diego'; R3: 'splashdown in the Pacific Ocean ... off the coast of San Diego'; R4: 'splashing down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego'
verifications.reasoning: All three sources explicitly confirm Pacific Ocean off San Diego.

verifications.claim: Artemis II lunar flyby is on April 6, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'today (April 6) ... looping around the far side of the moon'; R3: 'Moon Flyby ... April 6'; 'lunar flyby on Monday, April 6'
verifications.reasoning: Sources directly date the lunar flyby to April 6, 2026.

verifications.label: CLEAR

verifications.reasoning: All sources name or reference exactly four crew members.

verifications.claim: The goal of Artemis II is testing the Orion spacecraft systems with crew for the first time.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'first crewed flight of the SLS rocket and Orion spacecraft'; 'verify modern human capabilities in deep space'; R2: 'shakeout cruise designed to show that Orion can support astronauts in deep space'
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm first crewed test of Orion/SLS in deep space, matching the claim.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II capsule and crew will be recovered by US Navy and NASA teams after splashing down
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'NASA and U.S. Navy recovery teams'; 'USS John P. Murtha recovery ship'; R4: 'NASA’s Artemis Landing and Recovery team and U.S. Department of War personnel, including ... U.S. Navy divers ... USS John P. Murtha'
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly describe joint NASA and US Navy recovery post-splashdown.
